snippet.title: David and Goliath: The Shepherd Boy Who Killed a Giant
snippet.description: An entire army stood frozen in fear of one man — a giant nine feet tall who had humiliated them for forty days — until a shepherd boy too young for armour walked out to face him with nothing but a sling and five smooth stones. This is a cinematic recreation of David and Goliath from the Book of First Samuel: a valley of cowards, a giant's taunt, and the moment the smallest figure on the battlefield brought down the largest. Drawn faithfully from the Book of First Samuel. Welcome to Scripture On Screen.

snippet.title: Sodom and Gomorrah: The Cities God Burned to Ash
snippet.description: They were two cities so steeped in cruelty and corruption that their outcry reached heaven — and one of the only places in all of scripture that God destroyed completely, raining fire and burning sulphur from the sky until nothing was left but ash and a pillar of salt. This is a cinematic recreation of the fall of Sodom and Gomorrah from the Book of Genesis: Abraham's desperate bargain for the innocent, two angels at the gate, a family dragged from the flames, and the one woman who could not stop herself from looking back. Drawn faithfully from the Book of Genesis. Welcome to Scripture On Screen.

snippet.title: Samson and Delilah: The Strongest Man and the Woman Who Betrayed Him
snippet.description: He was the strongest man who ever lived — able to kill a lion with his bare hands and tear down the gates of a city — brought down not by an army, but by one woman, one secret, and one haircut. This is a cinematic recreation of Samson and Delilah, from the Book of Judges: a miraculous birth, a sacred vow, a fatal weakness for the wrong woman, and a blind, broken prisoner's final act of strength in the temple of his enemies. Drawn faithfully from the Book of Judges. Welcome to Scripture On Screen.

snippet.title: Noah's Flood: The Day the World Drowned
snippet.description: He was the only righteous man left in a world gone violent — and God told him to build a boat the size of a stadium, on dry land, for a flood that had never happened, while everyone he knew laughed. This is a cinematic recreation of the Flood from the Book of Genesis: a hundred years of ridicule, a door shut by the hand of God, the day the deep broke open and the world drowned, and the fragile promise that rose with a dove and a band of colour in the sky. Drawn faithfully from the Book of Genesis. Welcome to Scripture On Screen.

snippet.title: Ruth: The Foreign Widow Who Became a King's Bloodline
snippet.description: She was a foreigner, a widow, and a stranger to the God of Israel — and she gave up her home, her people, and her future to follow a bitter old woman who had nothing left to offer her. This is a cinematic recreation of the Book of Ruth: a famine, three graves in a foreign land, a vow spoken on an empty road, and an act of loyalty so complete that it wrote a penniless Moabite woman into the bloodline of King David himself. Drawn faithfully from the Book of Ruth. Welcome to Scripture On Screen.

snippet.title: The Red Sea: The Night God Split the Sea to Save a Nation
snippet.description: They were a nation of freed slaves, trapped against an impassable sea with the most powerful army on earth thundering down on them — no way forward, no way back, and one night to live or die. This is a cinematic recreation of the parting of the Red Sea, from the Book of Exodus: ten plagues, a midnight escape, six hundred war chariots in pursuit, a wall of water held back by the hand of God, and the morning a people walked out of slavery across the floor of the sea. Drawn faithfully from the Book of Exodus. Welcome to Scripture On Screen.

snippet.title: Daniel in the Lions' Den: The Night God Shut Their Mouths
snippet.description: He was the most trusted official in the most powerful empire on earth — and his rivals could find only one way to destroy him: make his faith against the law. This is a cinematic recreation of Daniel in the lions' den, from the Book of Daniel: a jealous conspiracy, a trap dressed up as a royal decree, an old man who kept praying anyway with his windows open, and a night in a pit of lions that proved whose hand really ruled the empire. Drawn faithfully from the Book of Daniel. Welcome to Scripture On Screen.

snippet.title: Leah: The Unloved Sister Who Became a Mother of Kings
snippet.description: She was the sister nobody chose — married by a trick to a man who loved someone else, and forced to spend her life beside a husband whose heart belonged to her younger sister. This is a cinematic recreation of the story of Leah, from the Book of Genesis: a wedding-night deception, a quiet ache for love that never came, and the God who saw the unwanted woman and made her, not her beautiful sister, the mother of kings and priests. Drawn faithfully from the Book of Genesis. Welcome to Scripture On Screen.

snippet.title: Joseph: The Boy His Brothers Sold Into Slavery
snippet.description: He was his father's favourite — the dreamer in the coat of many colours — and his own brothers hated him enough to throw him into a pit and sell him into slavery in a foreign land. This is a cinematic recreation of the story of Joseph from the Book of Genesis: a betrayal, a bloodied coat, a false accusation, a forgotten prisoner, and the dreams that carried a slave to the right hand of Pharaoh — and brought the brothers who sold him bowing to his feet. Drawn faithfully from the Book of Genesis. Welcome to Scripture On Screen.

snippet.title: Jezebel: The Most Wicked Queen in the Bible
snippet.description: She was a foreign princess who became queen of Israel — and used her throne to drag an entire nation into the worship of Baal, hunt down the prophets of God, and engineer the judicial murder of an innocent man for a plot of land. This is a cinematic recreation of the rise and fall of Queen Jezebel, from the Books of First and Second Kings: the fire on Mount Carmel, the vineyard of Naboth, the prophecy of the dogs, and the day a painted queen looked her killer in the eye. Drawn faithfully from First and Second Kings. Welcome to Scripture On Screen.

snippet.title: Job: The Man God Allowed Satan to Destroy
snippet.description: He was the greatest man in the East — blameless, upright, rich beyond counting, surrounded by a family he loved. And in a single afternoon, heaven made a wager over his soul and he lost everything: his wealth, his children, his health, stripped away while he was helpless to stop it. This is a cinematic recreation of the Book of Job — the oldest question humanity has ever asked, why the innocent suffer — and the man who lost it all and still would not curse God. Drawn faithfully from the Book of Job. Welcome to Scripture On Screen.

snippet.title: Esther: The Orphan Who Became Queen and Stopped a Genocide
snippet.description:
She was an orphan with a hidden name, raised by her cousin in a foreign empire — and she became the queen who walked, uninvited and under penalty of death, into the throne room of the most powerful man on earth to stop the slaughter of her people. 

This is a cinematic recreation of the Book of Esther: a stolen crown, a genocide signed into law by the king's right hand, a gallows built for the wrong man, and the night a hidden queen gambled everything on a single walk across a marble floor. 

Drawn faithfully from the Book of Esther, with the ancient feud of Amalek from Exodus, Deuteronomy, and First Samuel. Welcome to Scripture On Screen.
